title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
why_read: An ambitious new benchmark testing whether AI agents can conduct full physics research end-to-end, revealing current models fall far short of expert-level rigor.
analysis: FrontierPhysics is built from 56 real research tasks contributed by 42 practicing physicists, requiring an AI agent to review literature, plan experiments, run them, and write up results like a scientific manuscript. Unlike narrower benchmarks that only test isolated subtasks, this evaluates the entire research pipeline and judges whether outputs would actually be publishable. Testing 22 models in 26 configurations, the best setup passed fewer than a third of its trials, with failures traced mainly to weak reasoning rigor and lack of expert intuition rather than missing facts. This gives a sobering, well-grounded picture of how far AI agents are from genuinely automating scientific research.
